description: Stopped the run, changed agent/llm_client.py failover policy (a daily-quota 429 now fails over to the next model immediately and that model is skipped for the rest of the run, instead of walking a 15/30/60/120s backoff ladder first), then relaunched the supervisor. The orchestrator resumed from its checkpoint.
reason: Every LLM call was spending ~225s backing off against an exhausted daily quota before failing over, at ~3 calls per iteration. This is a change to the agent's BEHAVIOUR, not merely restarting a crashed process, so by the organizer's definition (Track 2 workshop Q&A, 2026-08-31: 'we only consider the manual intervention if you change the agent's behaviour') it counts as a manual intervention and is recorded as one.

description: Between agent runs, added an EXTRA_CATEGORICAL_FIELDS registry to pipeline/data/features.py and made pipeline/train.py resolve its encoded field list from it (stored per-run in id_maps['fields']).
reason: The second agent run proved its feature hypotheses were no-ops: two different patches adding a video-quality prior to features.py both scored EXACTLY 0.6024, because the new column was never encoded — CATEGORICAL_FIELDS lived in train.py, a different file, and a patch is one whole-file rewrite. The agent could not fix this itself within its own edit model. Verified after the change that the same hypothesis now moves the score (0.6027). This changes the agent's capability, so by the organizer's definition (Track 2 workshop Q&A 2026-08-31) it is a manual intervention and is recorded as one.
